IBO 2022 was the last online IBO, held remotely due to lingering COVID restrictions. All practical stations were adapted for remote delivery.

Final Medal Tally

How the medals fell

Gold
26
Silver
34
Bronze
71

No Merit category was awarded in 2022. The medal rate was 55.3% (131 out of 237), with 106 competitors receiving no award.

The Odds

What it actually took to medal in 2022

Top of the Podium

Only 1 in 9 competitors (11.0%) won Gold. The scoring system used normalized Z-total scores with a 50-point base, giving the final scores a mean near 50.

Medal Cutoffs

Where the lines were actually drawn

Final Z-total score range needed to earn each award

Gold
74.28 -- 92.39
Silver
63.00 -- 73.74
Bronze
46.04 -- 59.44
Wide Gold band

The Gold range spanned 18.11 points (74.28 to 92.39), the widest of any medal tier. By contrast, the Silver band was only 10.74 points wide. The top Gold medalists separated themselves decisively from the rest of the field.

By the Numbers

How hard was each station, really?

Average points earned vs. each lab's 100-point maximum

53%

37%

29%

Zoology was brutal

At just 29.4% average attainment, Zoology was the hardest practical station in any year of our 2022-2024 analysis. Over 70% of the points in this station went uncollected. Even Gold medalists averaged well below half marks.

Biochemistry: the perennial struggle

Biochemistry at 37.2% continues its pattern as one of the hardest stations across all years. The only station to score lower was Zoology in this same competition.

Team Standings

Top 15 delegations by medal count

11Bulgaria11266.2
12Hungary11263.5

14Czech Republic10259.7
15South Korea03162.9
Online format, different results

The online format produced a notably different leaderboard than in-person years. Iran achieved a 4-Gold sweep (ranked 7th-18th), a result they have not replicated in-person since. The Independent Olympiad Delegation also swept Gold, led by the competition's overall winner.

Theory vs. Practical

Some teams live on paper, others in the lab

India's 1-Gold team built their edge almost entirely on theory. The Netherlands showed the most extreme reverse pattern: their team dramatically outperformed in practicals relative to their theory scores.

Curiosities

4 things the official result does not say out loud

01
29.4% Zoology

The Zoology station's 29.4% average attainment is the lowest for any practical station across our entire 2022-2024 dataset. Even the median competitor captured less than a third of the available points.

02
Online advantage?

IBO 2022 was conducted online. The practical stations were adapted for remote delivery, which likely changed the skill mix required. Some traditionally strong in-person teams underperformed, while teams with strong computational skills found the format more natural.

03
r = 0.77

Theory-practical correlation was 0.77, the second-lowest in our 3-year window (2024 was 0.71). The online format may have made the practical component test a somewhat different skill set than theory.

04
No Merit awarded

Unlike 2023 and 2024, IBO 2022 did not award Merit certificates. The cut was binary: you either medaled (Bronze or above) or received nothing. This made the Bronze cutoff (46.04) effectively the pass/fail line.

For 2023 Hopefuls

What the data says to train next

1

Animal-focused practicals need real bench time

Zoology at 29.4% was devastating for most competitors. Dissection skills, specimen identification, and morphological analysis under time pressure cannot be learned from textbooks alone.

2

Biochemistry remains the bottleneck

At 37.2%, Biochemistry was the second-hardest station. This is a consistent pattern: Biochemistry ranks among the hardest stations in every year. Invest disproportionate training time here.

3

Theory is your floor, not your ceiling

Theory A and B both averaged ~73% attainment, meaning the theory exam was relatively accessible. To medal, you needed to perform well on theory AND find points in the more difficult practicals.

Independent analysis of the official IBO 2022 final results PDF. Not an official IBO publication.

Roughly 1 in 10 competitors (9.9%) won Gold. The medal rate (~52.6%) was significantly lower than IBO 2024's 84.2%, making 2023 a more selective year by that metric.

Gold-Silver gap

The Gold cutoff (123.12) sat 0.39 points above the best Silver (122.73). Even tighter than 2024's 0.53-point gap. One extra correct True/False statement on theory would have made the difference.

By the Numbers

Hardest to score on

Biochemistry had the lowest attainment rate at 45.8%, nearly 20 points below the easiest station (Plant Molecular Biology at 64.1%). Biochemistry is consistently one of the hardest IBO practicals across years.

Theory split

Theory Paper 2 (mean 184.8/230, 80.4% attainment) was substantially more accessible than Theory Paper 1 (mean 107.2/166, 64.6% attainment). The difference in difficulty between the two theory papers was larger than any practical station gap.

Singapore and India shine

Singapore and India both achieved perfect 4-Gold sweeps. Singapore's team average (132.3) was the highest of any delegation. India's 4-Gold haul at IBO 2023 was a historic result for the team.

Theory vs. Practical

Iran's 2-Gold team built their edge almost entirely on the theory exam, with the largest positive gap of any Gold-winning delegation. Kazakhstan, as the host nation, showed the opposite pattern: stronger in labs than on paper.

Curiosities

3 things the official result does not say out loud

01
r = 0.84

Theory and practical scores correlated at r = 0.84, the highest of any year in our 2022-2024 window. Competitors who tested well on paper almost always performed well in the lab. Being lopsided was the exception, not the rule.

02
Theory 2 was nearly twice as generous

Theory Paper 2 averaged 80.4% attainment vs. 64.6% for Paper 1. The 16-point gap is the largest theory-paper difficulty split in our dataset. If a competitor bombed Paper 1, Paper 2 was their lifeline.

03
Biochemistry bottleneck

Biochemistry was the hardest practical station at 45.8% attainment, nearly 20 points below the easiest station. This pattern repeats across all three years we analyzed: Biochemistry consistently punishes the field.

For 2024 Hopefuls

What the data says to train next

1

Theory and practicals move together

With r = 0.84, the 2023 data shows that broad competence matters. Pure theory grinders or pure lab rats rarely reached Gold. Build both.

2

Biochemistry is your ceiling

At 45.8% average attainment, Biochemistry is where most competitors left the most points on the table. Enzyme kinetics, assay interpretation, and wet-lab precision under time pressure are the highest-leverage training targets.

3

Master Plant Molecular Biology

PMB was the "easiest" station (64.1%), but that also means every Gold medalist scored well on it. If you cannot hold your own on the accessible stations, you cannot compensate elsewhere.

Independent analysis of the official IBO 2023 final results PDF. Not an official IBO publication.

Only 1 in 7 competitors (15.3%) walked away with Gold. The 84.2% medal rate was generous by IBO standards, but the gaps between tiers were razor-thin.

Medal Cutoffs

Where the lines were actually drawn

Razor-thin margins

The Gold cutoff (130.07) sat just 0.53 points above the best Silver score (129.54). The Silver-Bronze gap was similarly tight at 0.54 points. At this level, a single extra mark on one practical station would have changed medal colors.

By the Numbers

How hard was each station, really?

Hardest to score on

Bioinformatics had the lowest attainment rate of any station: competitors captured just 44.5% of its 100 available points. The station also had the second-highest correlation with final rank (r = 0.70).

Theory was king

Theory total (Papers A + B combined) correlated at r = 0.94 with final score, making it by far the single strongest predictor. Theory A averaged 63.1% attainment, Theory B averaged 61.3%.

Team Standings

Perfect teams

China, the United States, and Chinese Taipei are the only delegations where all 4 members won Gold. Vietnam came closest to joining them: 3 Gold and 1 Silver, with their Silver medalist finishing 17th overall.

Theory vs. Practical

Some teams live on paper, others in the lab

Average gap between theory T-score and practical T-score, by country (teams of 4 only)

Vietnam and China topped the overall medal table, and both built their edge disproportionately on the theory exam. Saudi Arabia and the Philippines showed the reverse: their teams outperformed their theory scores in the lab, suggesting strong practical training programs despite lower theory throughput.

Curiosities

4 things the official result does not say out loud

01
r = 0.94

Theory total correlated at 0.94 with final score. No single practical station came close (the highest was Molecular Biology at 0.71). If you had to predict someone's final rank from one number, their combined theory score would be right 94% of the way there.

02
0.53 points

The gap between the last Gold and the first Silver was 0.53 points. In a 165-point competition, that is 0.3% of the winner's score. A single extra True/False statement on either theory paper would have flipped the result.

03
Biochemistry was the "easy" lab

With 67.7% average attainment, Biochemistry was the most accessible practical station by a wide margin. Bioinformatics (44.5%) was the hardest. The 23-percentage-point gap between the easiest and hardest station is one of the largest in recent IBO history.

04
Pengbo Li: +2.10 theory-practical gap

China's #2 finisher (overall rank 2, final score 160.11) had the single largest theory-over-practical gap of any competitor. His theory T-score was 2.10 standard deviations above his own practical average, yet he still finished second overall. Pure theory dominance at the very top of the field.

For 2025 Hopefuls

What the data says to train next

1

Theory decides more than any single lab

Theory alone correlates r = 0.94 with final score. Master your written exam first. Every other component trails behind.

2

Bioinformatics was the differentiator

At 44.5% average attainment, most competitors struggled with the Bioinformatics station. Spending targeted time on sequence analysis, phylogenetic tools, and computational biology gives you the most room to gain points where others lose them.

3

Just short of a medal? Here is the fix

Merit to Bronze: The gap was just 0.30 points. A steadier finish across all four labs, not one breakthrough topic, is usually what closes that gap.

Bronze to Silver: 0.54 points. Hunt for lost partial-credit marks on the theory paper before you hunt for new topics.

4

Build a full team, not one star

Every Gold-sweep delegation (China, USA, Chinese Taipei) medaled with all 4 members. Depth wins team results.

Independent analysis of the official IBO 2024 final results PDF. Not an official IBO publication.

Only 1 in 10 competitors (10.1%) walked away with Gold. The 60.1% medal rate was moderate by IBO standards, and the gaps between tiers were the tightest in recent memory.

Record-tight margins

The Gold cutoff (82.21) sat just 0.38 points above the best Silver score (81.83). Silver-Bronze was even tighter at 0.28, and Bronze-Merit was 0.21. These are among the slimmest gaps in IBO history: a single extra mark on one station would have changed medal colors for dozens of competitors.

By the Numbers

Ecology & Systematics was the toughest station: competitors captured just 74% of its 70 available points. It also had the lowest correlation with final rank (r = 0.66), making it the most "unpredictable" station where strong students sometimes stumbled.

Theory was king (again)

Theory total (Papers 1 + 2 combined) correlated at r = 0.94 with final score. Theory 1 averaged 78% attainment, Theory 2 averaged 72%. The combined theory score averaged 57.2 out of 76.4 maximum (75%).

Team Standings

Gold sweeps

China and Singapore are the only delegations where all 4 members won Gold. China's team averaged 94.8, the highest of any delegation by a margin of 6 points. Singapore's 4-Gold showing is a significant rise from IBO 2024 (where they earned 2G 2S).

Theory vs. Practical

Some teams live on paper, others in the lab

Average gap between theory z-score and practical z-score, by country (teams of 4 only)

Stronger in Theory

Vietnam had the largest team-level theory advantage in 2025, finishing 1.08 standard deviations higher on theory than on practical. China and the United States followed a similar pattern. On the practical side, North Macedonia and Croatia built their performances disproportionately in the lab.

Curiosities

4 things the official result does not say out loud

01
r = 0.942 and r = 0.942

Theory z-score and practical z-score correlated with final score at exactly the same strength: 0.942. This is a rare perfect balance. In most IBO years, theory dominates. In 2025, if you wanted to predict someone's final rank, theory and practical performance were equally useful.

02
0.21 points

The gap between the last Bronze and the first Merit was just 0.21 points. In a 98.48-point competition, that is 0.2% of the winner's score. A single miscounted colony on a microbiology plate would have changed the outcome.

03
Ecology was the wildcard

Ecology & Systematics had the lowest correlation with final rank (r = 0.66) of any component. Strong students sometimes bombed it; weaker students sometimes aced it. It was the most unpredictable station, with just 74% average attainment. If you studied for this station specifically, you had a statistical edge others did not.

04
Zhiyuan Wu: +1.52 theory-practical gap

China's 3rd-place finisher had the largest individual theory-over-practical gap in the entire field. His theory z-score was 1.52 standard deviations above his own practical average, yet he still finished 3rd overall (score 94.9). Pure theory dominance at the very top of the field.

For 2026 Hopefuls

What the data says to train next

1

Theory and practical matter equally

Both correlated at r = 0.94 with final score. Do not neglect either. A balanced study plan that alternates between written problems and hands-on lab work is the statistical optimum.

2

Ecology & Systematics was the differentiator

At 74% average attainment, it was the station where most competitors left points. Spending targeted time on field ecology, species identification, and cladistics gives you the most room to gain where others lose.

3

The margins are vanishingly small

Merit to Bronze: 0.21 points. A steadier finish across all four labs is what closes this gap.

Bronze to Silver: 0.28 points. Focus on partial-credit marks on the theory paper before hunting new topics.

Silver to Gold: 0.38 points. At this level, it is about avoiding any single bad station.

4

Cell & Molecular Biology was the easiest points

With 82% average attainment, CMB was the most accessible station. Make sure you are not leaving free points here. Then invest extra time where the field struggles: Ecology (74%) and Theory Paper 2 (72%).

Independent analysis of the official IBO 2025 final results PDF. Not an official IBO publication.

Theory still dominates

Theory correlated at r = 0.96 with the composite final score. Theory Paper A averaged 71% attainment (33.0 / 46.4 max), Theory Paper B averaged 72% (32.4 / 44.8 max). Both papers were more accessible than any practical station.

Four-way Gold sweep

For the first time in recent IBO history, four delegations placed all 4 members in Gold: China, the United States, Chinese Taipei, and South Korea. China led with an average score of 91.1, nearly 5 points clear of the next team. South Korea's full-team Gold sweep is a notable rise from 2025 (where they placed 1G 2S 1B).

Theory vs. Practical

Some teams live on paper, others in the lab

Average gap between theory z-score and practical z-score, by country (teams of 4 only)

The United States built their 4-Gold sweep on theory strength, finishing +0.79 standard deviations better on theory than on practical. Luxembourg showed the most extreme practical advantage at -1.16: their team outperformed their theory baseline dramatically in the lab. India, despite earning 1G 3S, showed a large practical lean (-0.87), suggesting their lab training is substantially stronger than their theory preparation.

Curiosities

4 things the official result does not say out loud

01
4 Gold sweeps

China, the United States, Chinese Taipei, and South Korea each put all 4 team members in Gold. That is the most simultaneous Gold sweeps in recent IBO history. The "big four" combined for 16 of the 33 Gold medals (48.5%).

02
52% on Molecular Biology

The Molecular Biology practical was the hardest station competitors faced in 2026: the field captured barely half the 100 available points. Scores ranged from 3 to 100, one of the widest spreads of any IBO station in recent years. The top 33 Gold medalists averaged 77.7 on this station versus the field average of 51.9.

03
Plant Comparative Biology: r = 0.889

Among the four practical stations, Plant Comparative Biology had the strongest correlation with final rank (r = 0.889). It was also the station with the smallest maximum score (58 points), yet it was the best single-station predictor of overall performance. Students who excelled here tended to excel everywhere.

04
The largest IBO since 2019

With 302 competitors from 78 countries, IBO 2026 was the largest edition since pre-pandemic times. The field was 4 competitors larger than 2025 (298) and nearly 50% larger than the 2024 edition (203). The growing field did not dilute medal quality: the Gold cutoff was still tightly contested at 75.73.

For 2027 Hopefuls

What the data says to train next

1

Theory decides the podium

Theory correlated r = 0.96 with final score. Master your written exam first. Theory papers averaged 71-72% attainment, making them the most accessible component, but the range between best and worst was what separated medal tiers.

2

Molecular Biology was the differentiator

At 52% average attainment, most competitors struggled badly with the Molecular Biology practical. Spending targeted time on gel electrophoresis, PCR technique, cloning protocols, and molecular lab skills gives you the most room to gain where others lose.

3

Plant Biology is the stealth predictor

Plant Comparative Biology had the strongest single-station correlation (r = 0.889) with final rank. Botany, plant anatomy, and comparative morphology are often neglected in favor of molecular or animal biology, yet they predicted success better than any other station in 2026.

4

No easy stations to coast on

The highest station attainment was just 60% (Plant Comp. Biology). Every station was hard. Build competence across all four rather than banking on one strength. In 2026, nobody medaled by acing a single station alone.

Key trends

IBO 2024 was an outlier with its 84.2% medal rate; the 2025 and 2026 editions returned to the historic ~60% range. The field has been growing steadily: 302 competitors in 2026 is the largest in recent memory, up from 203 in 2024. Meanwhile, the Gold-Silver gap has tightened from 0.54 (2022) to 0.32 (2026). Getting to the top is harder than ever.

2025 was the most accessible year

IBO 2025 had the highest average station attainment of any year: three of its four stations sat above 80%. By contrast, IBO 2026 had no station above 60%, and Molecular Biology (52%) was the hardest single station since 2022's Zoology (29%).

South Korea's rise

South Korea went from 0 Gold (2022) to a perfect 4G sweep in 2026, the most dramatic improvement of any delegation over five years. Turkiye has steadily climbed from all-Silver (2022) to consistent 2G finishes.

The consistent powerhouses

Iran and Singapore earned Gold every single year from 2022 to 2026, never falling below 2G in any edition. China has been perfect (4G) in every year they competed (2023-2026). India earned at least 1G in all five years.

The Gold-Silver gap keeps shrinking

The Gold-Silver gap has narrowed from 0.54 (2022) to 0.32 (2026). In 2025, the Bronze-Merit gap was just 0.21 points, the tightest boundary in our five-year window. At the IBO level, medal color is increasingly decided by margins smaller than a single True/False question.

What We Learned

6 patterns that hold across every year

1

Theory is the best predictor of final rank

Correlation has risen from 0.77 (2022) to 0.96 (2026) and has never dipped below 0.77 in five years. No practical station comes close. Prioritize written exam mastery above all else.

2

Practical difficulty varies wildly between years

Average station attainment has ranged from 29% (Zoology 2022) to 82% (Cell & Mol Biology 2025). Prepare for stations at every difficulty level. A year with easy labs (2025: 80% avg) is followed by a year with hard ones (2026: 56% avg).

3

The Gold-Silver gap is never more than half a point

0.54, 0.39, 0.53, 0.38, 0.32 across five years, and trending down. Medal color at the top is decided by margins that amount to a single question. Accuracy under pressure matters more than breadth of knowledge.

4

Complete teams beat individual stars

Every Gold-sweep delegation across all five years had all 4 members medal. In 2026, four teams achieved the perfect 4G sweep simultaneously. Winning programs invest in depth, not a single standout.

5

The field is growing and getting more competitive

From 203 competitors (2024) to 302 (2026), and from 66 countries to 81 (2025). More nations are sending teams, and the medal boundaries have tightened despite the larger field. Each year it takes more to earn each tier.

6

China has been dominant since returning

Since re-entering in 2023, China has never placed fewer than 3 Gold, and achieved 4G in three consecutive years (2024-2026). Their average team score has consistently been the highest of any delegation.
